B.name: Trace back
B.shape: a claim everyone repeats → "who said it first?" → walk back link by link → reach a measurement, or reach nothing

C.name: One journey
C.shape: one continuous move from A to B; facts arrive as the camera passes them → land at the destination

D.name: Side by side
D.shape: two things, at true scale → the whole video closes the gap between what the viewer assumes and what the ruler says

E.name: The picture lies
E.shape: the subject is the DEPICTION (or the wording), not the thing depicted → what is drawn or written contradicts what is measured

F.name: Crossing the border
F.shape: something arrives → expensive and foreign → gets modified → becomes local identity

G.name: A recurring deadline
G.shape: a duty falls due again and again → the run of times it was missed → what breaks is not money but a relationship

H.name: Explain it
H.shape: set the problem → build it up layer by layer → the hardest part is EXPLAINED, not hidden → close on the thing worth remembering

I.name: The record changed, the world did not
I.shape: a record everyone knows → it changed value on a DATE → nothing in the world moved, only the definition → close on: what are we measuring?

J.name: What was lost
J.shape: the place → what it was → how it was lost → what it left behind, each piece standing alone → close on a new idea

K.name: Argument
K.shape: show ONE sentence everyone has heard → "how many holes does it have?" → hole one, two, three, each with a name and an everyday comparison → summary card → one verdict

L.name: News explainer
L.shape: an event with a date and a number → "why?" → the trigger everyone sees → root causes layer by layer, each with measured evidence → what is being done, with a date → close on what the viewer takes away for next time

M.name: Change one word
M.shape: a sentence the viewer says in their own head → let them hear it once → the fault is not the feeling but the LABEL → change exactly ONE word → measure → state the limits → close

N.name: Talking to one person
N.shape: something in the viewer is misunderstood → why it EXISTS (a function, not a fault) → why it overshoots (design, not breakage) → what it costs → change its MEANING, distinct from changing its label → the clinical line → close

O.name: Reading a graph
O.shape: a character or scene gives the feeling → name the phenomenon → explain it through the scene → place the character on ONE chart → add a second line or point on the same chart → close back on the character and the name

P.name: Empty world, late reveal
P.shape: a person alone inside one scene with no map → time counted by objects in a corner → events happen in the same world → only at the end the camera pulls out to reveal where they were all along

Q.name: Line and two clocks
Q.shape: the arrival, and the gap between plan and reality → the rules set at the start → the line drawn leg by leg → two year-clocks run: planned vs actual, labelled MOVING / WAITING → close on the gap in one sentence

R.name: One small moment, then pull out
R.shape: one small, human moment (a nap, a missed signal) → how things got there → the moment unfolds in one illustrated place, a time-of-day clock in the corner → the consequence → pull out to the big map and fill what was lost

S.name: Name the feeling
S.shape: a scene everyone recognises makes the viewer feel something → name it (and its translation) → where the image came from → what the word means → why it causes the feeling → the real origin revealed → close: next time you feel it, you'll know its name

T.name: Old story, new face
T.shape: a famous modern scene → a phenomenon named after an old story → tell the old story → map the modern figure onto it → one measured result → return to the scene, then hand a question back
